## Audit note (epic 3405-c0b7) — refined-bar guidance may resolve this deferred design decision

Re-triaging under the sharpened standard: an error code need not be narrow; prefer an **existing broad-but-accurate** code over new vocabulary, and reserve escalation for when NO existing code fits.

Applying that here: `ExpressionError` (execute-time input/step-output/loop-var/secret/env resolution failures) is not a provider-availability condition, so `llm_unavailable` MIS-fits it. The honest existing-vocab fit is **`command_failed`** ("an unclassified rebar command failure") — which accurately describes an execute-time wiring/resolution failure without asserting an outage.

This also dissolves the dbca-AC3 tension you flagged ("keep execute-time on llm_unavailable to protect genuine outages"): the correct discriminator is the exception TYPE, not the phase. Narrow `error_code_for` branch 6 to fire `llm_unavailable` only for `LLMUnavailableError` — then a genuine execute-time provider outage (raised as `LLMUnavailableError`) STILL maps to `llm_unavailable`, while `ExpressionError` (a `WorkflowError`, not an availability fault) falls to `command_failed`. No new vocabulary, no phase special-casing.

Suggest this may be **downgradable from an escalate/design-decision to ready-to-fix** (target code `command_failed`), unless an operator wants a finer `workflow_invalid`/`expression_unresolved` code — which the refined bar says to add only on demonstrated observable need. Not transitioning this ticket myself (read-only audit); flagging for the owner. See the observable sibling 7d47 (render_workflow, load-time) and the unifying recommendation on 5f96.
